statements.quote: We took advantage of the delayed introduction of ChatGPT in Egypt and conducted a pre-registered field experiment with nearly 100 senior university students at a public university.
statements.locator: Saved bioRxiv preprint, PDF p. 2, Abstract, lines 31-32.

statements.quote:
To explore this question, we conducted a pre-
registered field experiment with nearly 100 senior university students at a public university in Egypt where we tested the effect of using ChatGPT over a month in doing assignments on three dependent variables usually assumed by the literature to be AI-collaterals: innovation, risk behaviour, and readiness to exert effort.
statements.locator: Saved bioRxiv preprint, PDF p. 3, I. Introduction, lines 56-60.

statements.quote: We conducted a pre-registered field experiment in which 94 senior students from an Egyptian public university participated.
statements.locator: Saved bioRxiv preprint, PDF p. 7, III. Methods, lines 154-155.

statements.quote: A screenshot of the consent form presented before the commencement of the actual experiment can be found as part of the experimental script in the supporting documents.
statements.locator: Saved bioRxiv preprint, PDF p. 9, III. Methods, lines 196-198.

statements.quote: This ensured that participants did not provide any identification during the experiment or on the computers to protect their anonymity and that the experimenters had official signed documentation of participation (so no participant would be allowed to enter the experiment again).
statements.locator: Saved bioRxiv preprint, PDF p. 9, III. Methods, lines 200-203.

statements.quote: See S1 for the experimental script.
statements.locator: Saved bioRxiv preprint, PDF p. 11, III. Methods, lines 238-239.

statements.quote: Data across sessions was compiled and cleaned. After performing initial outlier analysis, two anomalous observations were detected in the dataset, and we decided to remove them based on interquartile range method (1.5xIQR rule).
statements.locator: Saved bioRxiv preprint, PDF p. 12, IV. Results, lines 254-256.

statements.quote: We also ran other tests tracing innovation that however produced insignificant results. These can be found in appendix II.
statements.locator: Saved bioRxiv preprint, PDF p. 14, IV. Results, lines 300-301.

statements.quote: Fig 5 shows the sheet given to subjects at the beginning of the session if they wanted to record their choices and profits over the rounds.

statements.quote: On caveats, despite the focus of the paper and its pre-registered hypothesis on possible negative effects of ChatGPT, it is still important to highlight that AI applications and AITGs are also likely to have significant advantages.
statements.locator: Saved bioRxiv preprint, PDF p. 16, V. Discussion, lines 361-363.

deposits.notes: Project title: Supplementary Material for "Is ChatGPT Detrimental to Innovation?". Found with the OSF title-filter query detrimental; the full article-title query missed this shorter project title. The contributor API identifies paper coauthor Engi Amin. Landing page, node metadata, osfstorage listing, children, providers, contributors, wiki, linked nodes and registrations all returned HTTP 200. The API reports public=true and current_user_permissions=[read]; access_requests_enabled=true does not make these public files restricted. There are three files, one storage provider, no subfolders in the file listing, and no children, linked nodes, registrations or linked registrations. node_license is null; no data license was found. Raw Data.xlsx was downloaded from https://osf.io/download/tvwcq/ (HTTP 200; 68948 bytes) and read in memory. Its Data sheet has 94 rows and 106 columns; Codebook has 106 variable-description rows and columns Variable, Description, Values. Each Data row contains one participant's repeated-round observations in wide format. Treatment values are ChatGPT (51 rows) and Control (43 rows). Subject_W_Session alone is not globally unique (13 distinct values); Date + Session + Server + Lab + Subject_W_Session yields 94 distinct, nonmissing participant keys. Numeric R1-R7_SugarConcentration, R1-R7_LemonConcentration and R1-R7_Price fields provide all seven rounds needed to derive the strategy-exploration outcomes S1-O2 through S1-O5. They are raw inputs, not deposited final innovation scores: has_outcome_scores=false refers to the absence of precomputed S1-O1 through S1-O5 scores, including all four coders' creativity ratings. Other measured outcomes such as Effort(out of 56) and Risk are present. R1_Message through R7_Message contain 658 nonempty message cells attached to participant rows, in English and Arabic; the codebook identifies P_Message and other P_ fields as practice-round variables. No intervention essays were deposited. No coder/rating, final creativity/innovation score, inclusion/exclusion or outlier flag columns were found, and no analysis code is listed. The 94 raw rows must not be substituted for the paper's 93-person descriptive sample or 91-person regression sample. The missing payout record and subsequent outliers cannot be identified with certainty from a deposited flag. The publicly downloadable preregistration PDF (https://osf.io/download/jufbp/, HTTP 200; 182850 bytes) is a one-page copy of AsPredicted #132739, Effects of Chat GPT, created 2023-05-19 05:53 AM (PT), and links to https://aspredicted.org/JZ5_PV4. The filename and document are labelled for peer review, but no account or access request was needed. Ethics committee approval.pdf also downloaded publicly (https://osf.io/download/8db79/, HTTP 200; 576759 bytes); it is a one-page PDF with no extractable text. The S1 experimental script and appendix II cited by the saved paper are not among the three files.

Discovered through the preregistration PDF in the OSF project found by title search. Public registration Effects of Chat GPT, #132739, dated 2023-05-19 05:53 (PT); author names remain anonymous for blind peer review, and the page says there are four authors. The record and its Download PDF link returned HTTP 200 without credentials; the generated PDF is one page, 196644 bytes. The stable View URL https://aspredicted.org/fnbp-6xd3.pdf returned HTTP 200 with HTML rather than PDF; the observed Download PDF link returned application/pdf with the filename recorded above. This is the same registration as the older OSF copy, not a second study or dataset. Questions 3 and 5 list risk, business-decision innovation and creativity of marketing messages, with outside coders for creativity; no primary-outcome hierarchy is labelled. Question 6 specifies exclusion of subjects not submitting prior assignments. The registration supplies no participant records, realized arm assignments, coder scores, exclusion identities, analysis code, laboratory AI-access instructions, or complete experimental script. It resolves the missing registration identifier but not the missing analysis data or protocol details.

Search false positive for research data: this is the external PREreview of the paper by Josie L. Otto, Bertha Mendoza and two other reviewers, not an author dataset or experimental-materials package. materials_only here denotes a review document. DataCite returned both the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.13138507 and version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.13138508; they resolve to this single record and are counted once. Both DOI landing URLs and both named record API URLs returned HTTP 200. The API listed only review.html (3033 bytes), and https://zenodo.org/api/records/13138508/files/review.html/content returned HTTP 200; its entire text was read in memory. It contains commentary on the paper, not participant texts or outcome data. The review observes that the preprint mentioned supplemental materials and an appendix without attaching them. It does not provide the missing script, appendix, ratings or analysis code.

what_we_could_compute: For S1-O3, S1-O4 and S1-O5, derive each participant's within-person variation in lemon concentration, sugar concentration and price from R1-R7 numeric choices; derive the average of these component SDs for S1-O2 under an explicitly stated SD convention. The deposited raw data support arm means, between-participant SDs, descriptive SEs and counts for that reanalysis. They do not identify the exact exclusions or standardization used for the paper's published 91-person analyses.

For the count-related open item, confirm the deposited raw sample as 94 participant rows: ChatGPT 51 and Control 43, with complete R1-R7 numeric choices and messages. Outcome-specific analysis counts can be computed for a documented reanalysis; the original post-exclusion arm counts, excluded participant identities and original slogan-analysis sample remain unconfirmed.

For the slogan data and aggregation open item, preserve participant membership using the unique Date + Session + Server + Lab + Subject_W_Session key and reshape R1_Message through R7_Message into participant-round outputs. Compute new participant-level text features and within-arm or between-arm diversity from 658 nonempty message cells, accounting for repeated unchanged slogans and both English and Arabic text. P_Message is explicitly the practice round and can be excluded. The original coder-score means, SDs, SEs, coder aggregation, rating-scale lower bound, paper's 265-message analysis corpus and original test rows cannot be recovered from the posted workbook because coder ratings and analysis code are absent.

The aggregate-strategy computation and raw-scale open item is partly addressable: the Codebook documents the three continuous choices on 0-10 scales and distinguishes practice from rounds 1-7. Raw-score and explicitly defined standardized reanalyses are possible. The authors' precise SD convention, any between-participant standardizer, figure error-bar definitions, unlabeled regression quantities and inference appropriate to course-level assignment remain unresolved.
notes: Public participant-level raw outcome data and arm assignment were confirmed by reading the workbook, not inferred from a repository title. public_participant_data applies because numeric trial measurements underlying S1-O2 through S1-O5 and participant-linked slogan outputs are public; it does not imply that precomputed creativity scores, coder ratings or the final analysis sample are available. Accordingly has_outcome_scores=false records the absence of deposited final scores, while the raw outcomes are sufficient to compute new strategy-exploration and diversity statistics. The whole 885-line markdown conversion was read, including its end matter and appended-page conversion; relevant statements were checked with PyMuPDF against the saved 32-page PDF. The saved source is the bioRxiv preprint posted April 5, 2024, DOI 10.1101/2024.04.03.588037, despite the 2026 filename. Quotes remove printed line numbers and normalize line-wrap whitespace; the split pre-registered word in the Introduction retains its line break. The saved paper has no explicit data/code availability or on-request statement, no repository or preregistration identifier, and no supplement download URL. The form's data_url and code_url are empty. Its supporting-documents, S1 and appendix II references are quoted above. The paper's acknowledgments contain thanks to instructors and laboratory staff, with no data-access statement. The repeated CC-BY 4.0 notice applies to the preprint, not automatically to the separately posted dataset; the printed license link http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ returned HTTP 200 and redirected to HTTPS. No dataset license was confirmed. Searching a shorter title term was necessary to discover the public OSF project. The AsPredicted identifier is now confirmed, but the script, appendix II, laboratory AI restrictions and course-allocation mechanism remain unverified. The later journal landing page was blocked by a bot check, so no claim is made about its supplementary inventory or changes from the saved preprint. All network requests used Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 and no email address or personal identifier. Files were read only in memory; no account, login, access request or bot-check bypass was attempted. The review-only Zenodo record and duplicate preregistration host are retained in deposits for an auditable record of checked resources; they add no participant data.
